title: Automated sample-driven verification and pin workflow for verified performance profiles
creator: Aisha Patel
description: Define and implement an automated, sample-driven pipeline that validates candidate model versions across a compact but representative workload sample, promotes stable candidates to 'Redwood-verified' profiles, and generates a signed pin artifact. The flow aims to minimize manual review while preserving safety and production reliability.
background: Current verified profile publication is semi-manual: benchmarks run in bulk and human reviewers check windows before publishing. This creates latency in onboarding and inconsistencies in rollout gating. We need a reproducible, auditable pipeline that makes high-confidence publish decisions for straightforward model upgrades and surfaces edge cases for manual review.
goals: Create a deterministic stratified sampling strategy (by sequence length, batch size, and prompt shape) that fits into a 2-hour verification window
Implement a lightweight smoke validator (micro-bench + shadow-run) that computes p50/p95 latency, throughput, and normalized cost-per-token
Automate pin signing and publish to the performance manifest when stability criteria pass
Provide operational visibility (dashboard and short-lived logs) and audit trail links for every automated publish
Reduce time-to-publish for low-risk model revisions from days to hours
success_metrics: 50% reduction in median time from model push to published verified profile for low-risk models
<1% false-positive publishes (automated publishes that require rollback within 72h)
>90% of automated publishes pass rollback safety checks and smoke canary in prod
Telemetry coverage: automated verification must exercise >= 80% of common seq-length buckets seen in production
scope: Design and implement sampling algorithm and sample-set generator
Lightweight benchmark runner (local micro-bench) plus distributed shadow-run harness
Stability rules and gating (e.g., rolling median p95 delta < 15% over 72h window)
Automated signing of verified profile artifacts and registry publish
Dashboard tile for automated publishes and last green commit
out_of_scope: Full-length end-to-end heavy benchmarks used by offline verification (these remain in parallel pipelines)
Automatic rolling of customer pins without tenant opt-in (enterprise policy separate)
Model architecture change approvals that require ML research sign-off
plan_steps: Define stratified sampling buckets from recent production telemetry (ENG to provide histograms)
Implement sample-set generator tool (pm/sample-gen) with reproducible seeds
Build micro-bench binary to measure p50/p95 latency and tokens/sec on candidate instances
Create shadow-run runner to replay a 1k-5k request sample against candidate version in staging
Define stability rules and implement gating service (rules: p95 within 15%, throughput within 10%, cost delta within 8%)
Wire automated sign-and-publish step that creates a signed JSON manifest and pushes to profile-registry with provenance links
Add dashboard and alerting: published-by-automation badge, last-automated-publish, quick-links to PRs and logs
Run a pilot on two low-risk open models and iterate on thresholds for 2 weeks
risks: Sampling may miss rare worst-case prompts leading to regressions in customer workloads
Overly permissive thresholds could publish regressions; overly tight thresholds block benign upgrades
Shadow-run overhead could impact staging cluster capacity if not throttled
Automated signing increases blast radius if gating rules are incorrect
mitigations: Require an explicit manual-review opt-in for models with high production usage or enterprise pins
Start with conservative thresholds and allow a configurable grace period per model family
Throttle shadow-run traffic and schedule during low-util windows; run smoke tests on dedicated canary nodes
Add multi-signer requirement for high-impact model families (configurable via registry policy)
dependencies: ENG-55821: production telemetry histograms export (seq_len, batch_size, prompt_shape)
ENG-57190: lightweight micro-bench binary and perf harness
ENG-58212: profile-registry API for signed artifact uploads
PM-7120: standardized verification tags and deprecation policy (policy alignment)
Console-2201: dashboard widget capability and short-lived log links
stakeholders: Engineering: Marco Nguyen (assignee), Priya Rao (perf team lead)
acceptance_criteria: Pipeline can generate deterministic sample-set from production telemetry and seed
Automated run produces a verification report (p50/p95/throughput/cost) and an explicit pass/fail decision
On pass, a signed artifact is published to the profile registry with provenance links to PRs, logs, and telemetry
Pilot: at least 2 model revisions successfully auto-published with no manual rollback after 72h
Owners can disable automation per-model via registry flag and require manual review
notes: We intentionally focus on compact representative workloads to save compute and review time; heavyweight validation lives elsewhere
Consider integrating Redwood Optimize hints into the verification report (suggested quantization/kv-cache settings)
Signed artifact format should include canonical perf vectors (small sample of inputs), runtime config snapshot, and the seed used to generate sample-set
Audit trail must include exact git SHA of benchmark harness and kernel/runtime versions used
